findings.title: Duplicate bridge-neck identity mapping
findings.why_it_matters: The harness binds thermal cases to PFC branches with a second private copy of each reviewed trace UUID and its segment suffix, while the thermal model separately owns the same trace-to-net mapping. A board repair that changes a selected neck must update both crates in lockstep; updating only the thermal model makes a successfully replayed assessment fail its later current binding, with no compiler-visible relation between the two mappings.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the thermal bridge-neck definition the single public mapping, including net, trace UUID, and the PFC branch identifier/prefix needed for binding. Have bridge_thermal derive NETS and branch lookup from that mapping, then add a test that each exported neck definition resolves exactly one PFC branch.

findings.title: Scattered mesh-tag protocol
findings.why_it_matters: The thermal pipeline encodes the terminal, far-face, and exterior boundary contract as raw numbers in the Gmsh generator, mesh verifier, Elmer transfer verifier, and SIF generator. Changing a boundary or adding one requires manually synchronizing four independently typed numeric protocols; a missed update can bind current or cooling to the wrong face without a type-level indication of the semantic mismatch.
findings.suggested_fix: Define named shared body and boundary tag constants (and, where practical, a BoundaryAreas struct keyed by terminal/far/exterior) in one thermal module. Generate the Gmsh and SIF text and validate Gmsh/Elmer tags through those names instead of separate 1/2/11/12/13 literals.
